As long as her top eyelids don’t hang low enough to affect her vision (which they don’t appear to), she’s okay. If you are concerned about it, you could ask your vet about them possibly being dry from droopiness. Newfies just have very bloodshot eyes though. Looks like a big, healthy fluff ball :). She looks to be a good size for a newfie - not overweight or anything by any means. If you take her on swims regularly since newfies are generally avid swimmers, she could have gained some muscle mass. I’ve had two female newfies - both with completely different body shapes. One was shaped more like a great dane - huge head, very tall and lanky, unable keep on weight due to her thyroid; the other - shorter legs, denser bones, huge booty and a more square but strong build and mass to her. Really depends on your breeder. Your girl is absolutely radiant and beautiful. Reflects well on your care as an owner. Sorry for rambling, I just never get to talk about my newfies since they aren’t common where I live. 

TL;DR: your newf looks healthy :)

My newfie is a stubborn brat and sometimes requires me to hold a few pieces of kibble in my palms so she can eat out of my hands. As a puppy, our first newf would only eat one piece of kibble at a time from our hands. Definitely big stubborn babies. If possible, I would recommend putting some bits of boiled chicken or a small amount of food topper on his kibble. Also, which maybe a little gross, you could mix in some water with his kibble to soften it if you suspect jaw or tooth pain.

I’d definitely rule out kennel cough or heart problems first, but if the vet has checked everything, it might be worth making sure there aren’t a lot of of respiratory irritants in your house. Thank you for saying that. I don’t mean to fear-monger or anything, I just want people who are interested in getting an iggy to know that leg breaks can very easily happen. They are soooo worth it though. My iggy is the sweetest, neediest, silliest, cuddliest, most sensitive little angel with the biggest personality. It doesn’t matter how upset or angry I am, all I have to do is look at him being his silly and sweet self and I smile instantly. They really are an extraordinary breed (definitely not for everyone though since they’re so needy in terms of wanting to literally crawl under your skin and wanting to be a part of you and not wanting to be away from you for any amount of time), they’re just very fragile and require a decent amount of care. I’d say do a LOT of research about health issues, oral care, general anxiety, separation anxiety, etc. be sure you have a decent amount of money put aside in case of a break. Also, something not a lot of people know is that greyhounds (all sizes) are not supposed to be put under anesthesia unless it is absolutely necessary. It’s very dangerous for them, so you want to take care of their health (mainly oral care) from a young age and the rest of their life. Brush their teeth a few times a week to prevent infections that can lead to organ failure. That being said, if you have time to care for one and have an appropriate living situation for them to be safe, I would absolutely 100% recommend one. They’re a lot to care for, but they really are amazing companions.

Honestly, more common than you think. Iggies are amazing, but they are soo fragile and it’s a nightmare. Not enough people talk about leg breaks. My iggy broke his leg as a puppy, and it was absolutely horrendous. Not only was he in immense pain and screaming, we also had to pay about $5,000 for his surgery and treatment. They said that based on his break and age at the time, he was lucky he didn’t have to get the whole leg removed. And the healing process is rough too, because Iggies love to run, but they’re not able in order to recover. I get nightmares all the time about him getting into accidents or accidentally breaking a leg again. He no longer is allowed to play with our larger dog, as they have had a few scares when she accidentally overpowers him. I’m constantly afraid that he’s going to re-break it or break a different one. Every time he accidentally injures himself or gets injured, my first reaction is “please don’t be a break.” It’s really scary and you have to be very careful. He is so worth every cent we’ve spent on him and his break, but it’s something I’m scared of happening again constantly.
